title: Light-Controlled Fermentations for Microbial Chemical and Protein Production
protocol: Obtain a strain with his3 auxotrophy.
Delete any endogenous copy of the gene to be regulated if it is native to S. cerevisiae.
Linearize the plasmid containing the OptoINVRT7 circuit at the PmeI restriction site.
Integrate the linearized plasmid into the his3-locus using lithium-acetate transformation methods.
Centrifuge the transformed cells at 150 x g for 1 min.
Resuspend the cells in 200 µL of SC-His medium.
Plate the resuspended cells onto SC-His agar plates.
Incubate the plates at 30 °C for 2-3 days until colonies appear.
Prepare competent cells from the selected strain using standard lithium acetate transformation protocols.
Transform the competent cells with a plasmid containing the gene(s) to be controlled downstream of either the PGAL1-M or PGAL1-S promoter.
Centrifuge the culture at 150 x g for 1 min.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 200 µL of fresh SC-dropout medium.
Plate the entire cell volume on a YPD agar plate if integrating into δ-sites, or an SC-dropout plate if transforming with a plasmid containing a selection marker.
Incubate at 30 °C for 16 h under constant blue light to keep the optogenetically controlled gene repressed.
Create a replica of the plate onto YPD plates containing a range of Zeocin concentrations between 400 µg/mL and 1,200 µg/mL.
Incubate the replica plates at 30 °C under constant or pulsed blue light for 2-3 days until colonies appear.
Select eight colonies from each plate.
Inoculate 1 mL of SC-His medium supplemented with 2% glucose in individual wells of a 24-well plate using selected colonies.
Grow cultures overnight at 30 °C with 200 rpm shaking under constant blue light illumination.
Dilute each culture to OD600 values ranging from 0.01-0.3.
Incubate diluted cultures in dark for 4 h at 30 °C with 200 rpm shaking by wrapping plates in aluminum foil.
Centrifuge the cultures in the 24-well plate at 234 x g for 5 min.
Resuspend cells in 1 mL of fresh SC-dropout medium with 2% glucose.
Seal the plates to prevent evaporation using sterile microplate sealing tape.
Ferment the sealed plates in the dark for 48 h at 30 °C with shaking at 200 rpm.
Wrap the plates in aluminum foil to prevent exposure to light.
Centrifuge the plates for 5 min at 234 x g to harvest the fermentations.
Transfer 800 µL of the supernatant into 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tubes.

Analyze using high-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC), gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS), or another suitable analytical method based on the sample preparation technique best suited for the instrument used.
Recover transformed cells for 1 h in 1 mL of SOC medium at 37 °C with rotation or shaking.
Centrifuge the cells at 4845 x g for 3 min.
Concentrate the pellet in 200 µL of LB media.
Plate concentrated cells onto an LB agar plate with appropriate antibiotics and grow overnight at 37 °C under constant blue light illumination.
Take three single colonies from the plate.
Use each colony to inoculate 1 mL of LB media with appropriate antibiotics in individual wells of a 24-well plate.
Grow overnight (16-20 h) at 37 °C with 200 rpm shaking under constant blue light illumination.
Measure OD600 of culture using spectrophotometer with microvolume measurement.
Dilute cultures into 1 mL of fresh LB in 24-well plates to OD600 values ranging from 0.01-0.1.
Grow cultures at 37 °C with 200 rpm shaking under blue light for 2-3 h.
Take OD600 measurements every 15 min starting from the second hour to ensure cultures do not overgrow in the range of OD600 0.1-1.5.
Once cultures reach the desired OD600, turn off the light panel and wrap the plate in aluminum foil to initiate the production phase.
Keep the plate in the dark for 8 h at 37 °C with shaking at 200 rpm.
Alternatively, keep the plate in the dark for 20 h at 30 °C with shaking at 200 rpm.
Or, keep the plate in the dark for 48 h at 18 °C with shaking at 200 rpm.
Measure and record the final OD600 value of each culture.
Transfer 800 µL of each culture into a 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube and centrifuge for 5 min at 17,000 x g.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 200 µL of resuspension buffer (Tris 50 mM, pH 8.0, NaCl 300 mM).
Add 50 µL of 6x sodium dodecyl sulfate (SDS) sample buffer to each tube.
Incubate at 100 °C for 10 min with shaking at 700 rpm in a thermomixer.
Load ~3-20 µL of the culture onto a 12% SDS-PAGE gel.
Use final OD600 measurement as a guide to load approximately the same amount of protein for each sample (equivalent to 10 µL of the sample corresponding to a final OD600 value of 1).
Run electrophoresis at 100 V until the gel is fully resolved.
Stain the gel with Coomassie brilliant blue G-250 solution by heating for 30-40 seconds in a microwave oven.
Incubate the stained gel on a platform rotator for at least 15 minutes.
Rinse the gel twice with deionized water.
Destain the gel on a platform rotator for at least 30 minutes (or overnight).
Add two cleaning wipes tied into a knot to help absorb the stain during destaining.
Boil the gel in sufficient water in the microwave oven for 15 minutes to speed up destaining.
Obtain a strain with a his3 auxotrophic marker.
Linearize a plasmid containing the OptoAMP4 circuit at the PmeI restriction site.
Integrate the linearized plasmid into the his3 locus of the auxotrophic strain using lithium-acetate transformation methods.
Centrifuge the cells at 150 x g for 1 minute after transformation.
Gently resuspend the cells in 200 µL of fresh SC-His medium.
Plate the entire cell volume on selective media (SC-His-agar).
Incubate the plated cells at 30 °C for 2-3 days until colonies appear.
Prepare competent cells from the strain with integrated OptoAMP4 circuit.
Transform these competent cells with a plasmid containing the gene(s) to be controlled optogenetically downstream of the PGAL1-S promoter.
Centrifuge the culture at 150 x g for 1 min.
Resuspend the centrifuged culture in 200 μL of fresh SC-dropout medium.
Plate the entire cell volume on a YPD or SC-dropout agar plate and incubate at 30 °C for 16 h in the dark (wrapped in aluminum foil).
Replica plate onto YPD plates containing a range of Zeocin concentrations to select for a variety of integration copy numbers.
Incubate the replica plates at 30 °C in the dark (wrapped in aluminum foil) for 2-3 days until colonies appear.
Select eight colonies from each plate and use them to inoculate 1 mL of SC-His medium with 2% glucose in individual wells of a 24-well plate.
Grow the cells overnight (16-20 h) in the dark at 30 °C with 200 rpm shaking.
Dilute each culture in 1 mL of fresh SC-His medium with 2% glucose to achieve an OD600 of 0.1.
Grow cultures in dark at 30 °C with 200 rpm shaking until they reach an OD600 of 3.
Incubate the plates under pulsed light (5 s on/95 s off) for 12 h at 30 °C with 200 rpm shaking using a 465 nm light source to achieve ~80-110 µmol/m²/s light intensity.
Centrifuge cultures at 234 x g for 5 min and resuspend in fresh SC-His medium with 2% glucose.
Seal the plates to prevent evaporation of the desired product using sterile microplate sealing tape.
Ferment sealed plates in light for 48 h at 30 °C with shaking at 200 rpm.
Centrifuge plates for 5 min at 234 x g and transfer 800 µL of supernatant into 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tubes.

Inoculate a colony of an E. coli strain engineered for light-controlled chemical production into 5 mL of M9 minimal salts supplemented with casamino acids, glucose, and trace metal mixture in a 50 mL conical tube.
Grow the culture overnight at 30 °C with 200 rpm shaking under blue light illumination.
Set up the bioreactor vessel head plate.
Install an insert for thermal probe.
Install a dissolved oxygen (DO) probe.
Connect the gas sparger to the air source through a 0.2 µm filter.
Install the impeller.
Connect the gas condenser to a 0.2 µm filter.
Set up two cooling lines.
Install feed lines for media addition and pH control.
Ensure the sampling line reaches the bottom of the vessel.
Install an empty port.
Calibrate the pH probe with standards of pH = 4 and pH = 7 prior to installation.
Autoclave or sterilize the vessel components before setup.
Fill the vessel with 1 L of filtered water.
Attach the head plate and tighten, ensuring the O-ring fits snugly and seals.
Cover any openings in the reactor with aluminum foil.
Prepare three strips of tubing: one for removing water, one for inserting feed, and one for pH control.
Cover the ends of the tubing with aluminum foil and wrap all tubing in aluminum foil.
Autoclave the bioreactor and tubing using a 30 min liquid cycle.
Remove materials from the autoclave once cooled.
Connect the impeller to the vessel.
Connect the pH and DO probes to the vessel.
Connect the air source to the vessel.
Connect the condenser inlet and outlet to the control station.
Connect the cooling inlet and outlet to the control station.
Insert the thermal probe into the vessel.
Cover the vessel with a heating jacket and secure it toward the top of the vessel.
Connect one sterile tube to the sampling line and secure through the sampling pump.
Place the other end of the sampling tube such that it flows into an empty container that can hold at least 1 L.
Drain the water inside the vessel.
Connect another sterile tube to one of the feed lines and secure through one of the feed pumps.
Connect the other end of the feed line to a bottle of M9 media.
Feed the media into the reactor.
Connect another sterile tube to one of the feed lines.
Secure the tube through one of the feed pumps.
Connect the other end of the tube to a bottle containing 28%-30% NH4OH.
Place three light panels in a triangular formation ~20 cm away from the reactor.
Check that the light intensities on the surface of the vessel reach ~80-110 µmol/m²/s from each side.
The next day, turn on the bioreactor system and chiller.
Set the reactor temperature setpoint to 37 °C.
Set the pH setpoint to 7.0.
Set the agitation speed to 200 rpm.
Calibrate the DO probe by waiting until temperature and DO measurements become constant.
Disconnect the probe from the system once the measurement stabilizes at 100%.
Repeat calibration until the DO measurement stabilizes at 100% when the probe is connected.
Set the DO setpoint to 20%.
Inoculate the bioreactor to an initial OD600 of 0.001-0.1.
Turn on the light panels to initiate growth.
Begin taking samples from the sampling line after 3 hours for OD600 measurements.
Turn off the light panels when the optimal ρs (optimal value for mevalonate production is 0.17) is reached.
Cover the reactor in aluminum foil and wrap it in black cloth to initiate the dark production phase.
Add 50 μL of antifoam directly into the reactor using the sampling port 8 hours after switching to darkness.
Unscrew the empty port and pipette the antifoam directly into the reactor.
Use the sampling port to periodically take samples for HPLC or GC analysis.
Turn off the system after the experiment is concluded.
Carefully unscrew the DO and pH probes and wash them with soap and water.
Unscrew the head plate and wash it with soap and water using a brush.
Transfer the culture into an empty container and add bleach to a final concentration of 10% v/v.
Place the container in a fume hood and dispose of it after 30 minutes.
Wash the reactor vessel with soap and water using a brush.
Prepare samples for analysis based on the product of interest.
Mix 560 µL of culture with 140 µL of 0.5 M HCl and vortex at high speed for 1 min to convert mevalonate into (±)-mevalonolactone.
Centrifuge at 17,000 x g for 45 min at 4 °C.
Transfer 250 µL of the supernatant to an HPLC vial.
Analyze samples using an organic acids ion exchange column.
Quantify production using a refractive index detector (RID).
Compare peak areas to a standard of (±)-mevalonolactone.
